Expand peptides onto every protein they map to

Source: R/prot-all.R
expand_mapped_proteins.Rd

A short, non-tryptic HLA ligand frequently maps to more than one protein. This returns the peptide-to-protein mapping implied by the search engine's own list of mapped proteins, one row per (peptide row, protein).

Usage

expand_mapped_proteins(input, protein = "ProteinFirst")

Arguments

input

A pep_all-shaped data frame.

protein

Column holding the leading protein. Default "ProteinFirst".

Value

input with the protein column replaced by one row per mapped protein, plus a logical Protein_shared marking peptides that mapped to more than one.

Details

The list lives in a different column per engine — FragPipe's Mapped_Proteins, DIA-NN's and PEAKS' Accession — with a different separator, so the source is resolved from the Found_By column. When the table carries no such list (PEAKS' peptide export, the custom-dictionary path, or a FragPipe run whose Mapped_Proteins is empty) the leading protein is returned with a warning, which is the same answer multi_mapping = "leading" would give.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
expand_mapped_proteins(pep_all)
} # }
